decisions.question: S94 ruled (would_have_asked, stop_class axis) that a phase of a node this intake did not re-plan counts as confirmed for a new contract version once its id is unchanged and its swept Consumes or Produces line names the new version, and on that basis flipped topology-dsl@v2, bus-api@v2, bus-testing@v2 and flutter-binding@v2 to stable and final. Does the orchestrator, deciding stops under DEC-686, accept the ruling?

options.label: Accept; all nine contracts stable and final
options.consequence: The tree is back to the state the run ended in at S53: every contract stable and final, gate.mjs --final clean but for historical references. nidana.model, nidana.tooling.codegen and nidana.tooling.lint keep plans written against v1 and swept to v2.

options.label: Re-plan the three nodes with hsdd-phase-plan append runs first
options.consequence: Three more steps and their reconciles; S77, S88 and S89 already checked that no guarantee those phases implement or replay changed beyond citations, so the runs would most likely emit the same confirms.

decisions.chosen: Accept; all nine contracts stable and final
decisions.why: Reconcile confirms phase ids, and the version bump changed none of these ids. The insert rule, written for exactly this case, was checked at each contract step and each node touch and never triggered for these three nodes; the sweep moved their citations under the S64 touch rule. Holding stable status hostage to three no-op re-plans would leave four stable-in-substance contracts marked draft for no consumer's benefit. The signal that would have changed my mind: any of S59 to S73 reporting a replay change in a nidana.model, codegen or lint phase.
